title: Have you not seen what your Lord did?
subtitle: A story everyone in Makkah remembered
then: Abrahah marched from Yemen with an elephant to destroy the Ka'bah. Abdul-Muttalib asked only for his camels back and said: {idea}I am the lord of the camels; the House has its Lord Who will defend it{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ was born that same year, by the most popular view, and {reward}the Makkans had seen it with their own eyes{/reward}.
now: You face something far bigger than you: a lawsuit, an illness, a company that wants your job gone. You have no army. {idea}Do what is yours to do, and leave the rest to its Lord.{/idea} This surah starts by asking you to remember that He acts.
old: If I cannot fix it myself, nothing will be done.
new: I take care of my camels. What belongs to Allah, Allah defends.
try: Write down one problem too big for you. Do your one small part, then hand the rest to Allah in dua.

title: Their whole plan came to nothing.
subtitle: The elephant knelt and would not move
then: They planned to tie chains to the Ka'bah and have the elephant pull it down. The tafsir reports that when turned toward Makkah, {idea}the elephant knelt and refused to rise{/idea}, yet walked quickly in every other direction. Allah {reward}made their efforts in vain{/reward}.
now: Someone at work is building a case against you. A rumour is spreading. You lie awake picturing every move they might make. {idea}Allah can make a plan kneel before it starts.{/idea} Your job is to stay upright, not to outplan everyone.
old: If someone is plotting against me, I am finished.
new: Plots can go astray in a moment. Allah can turn the strongest plan to nothing.
try: If someone is working against you, make dua for protection and refuse to plot back.

title: He sent birds, flock after flock.
subtitle: The smallest creatures against an army
then: The scholars said ababil means {idea}groups, one after another, coming from everywhere{/idea}. Several said they came from the sea. The people of Makkah were on the mountaintops, {reward}watching the birds arrive{/reward}.
now: Help rarely arrives the way you expected. Not the big break, but a stranger's text, a small refund, a nurse who stays late. {idea}Allah's help can come on small wings.{/idea} Watch for it.
old: Only something big and powerful can solve a big problem.
new: Allah can answer an army with birds. Help can come in the smallest form.
try: Tonight, list three small unexpected helps you received this month and thank Allah for each.

title: Pelting them with stones of baked clay.
subtitle: Tiny stones, total defeat
then: Each bird carried {idea}three stones the size of chickpeas and lentils{/idea}, one in each claw and one in the beak. Ibn Hisham said sijjil means something hard, from stone and clay. The army {trap}fled in panic{/trap} along every road.
now: You think your small dua cannot change a big situation. Your small coin cannot fix a big need. {idea}Size is not what gives a thing its force.{/idea} Allah put an army to flight with pebbles.
old: My small efforts are too tiny to make any difference.
new: When Allah wills, a pebble outweighs an army. My small effort can carry weight.
try: Make one short, sincere dua today for a big problem, and trust it is not too small.

title: Left like straw that cattle have chewed.
subtitle: How the proud army ended
then: Abrahah said, {trap}I cannot be prevented{/trap}. Sa'id bin Jubayr said asf is straw, and ma'kul the fodder cut for animals. Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}repelled them in their plan and their anger{/idea}. They achieved no good at all.
now: You have felt unstoppable: the promotion, the winning argument, the moment you thought nobody could touch you. {idea}This verse is a picture of where that feeling can end.{/idea} Humility now is cheaper than being humbled later.
old: When I am strong enough, nothing can stop me.
new: Strength without humility can end as chewed straw. I would rather stay humble.
try: The next time you feel sure of yourself today, say: if Allah wills.
